purpose: Canonical content model for Korean Review. Lesson packs, Explore systems, user-created study items, and future Media Lab content should map into these shapes instead of inventing new fields per feature.

fields.originNote: Use Hanja as a meaning clue; modern Korean and Mandarin usage may differ.

fields.name: Benefactive expression
fields.meaning: Do an action for someone’s benefit.

examples.en: I bought bread for my friend.

contrast.note: Both can appear in requests, but -아/어 주세요 explicitly frames the action as a favor/benefit.

commonMistakes: Do not translate 주다 literally as ‘give’ in every benefactive construction.

fields.pragmatics: Used when answering or initiating a phone call; not a general face-to-face greeting.

fields.title: Telephone etiquette
fields.summary: Korean phone conversations use conventional openings, polite requests, and relationship-sensitive endings.

fields.prompt: Choose the most natural expression for answering a phone call.
fields.explanation: 여보세요 is the conventional phone greeting.

fields.title: Korean Number Systems
fields.summary: Connect number rules across lessons instead of reteaching them separately.

principles: Keep sourceRefs for traceability but do not reproduce full copyrighted slides or textbook pages in the public site.
Use original explanations and original practice questions.
Vocabulary can have Hanja/Chinese clues only when the relationship is supportable; do not label every word as Chinese-derived.
Audio, images, examples, and translations are enrichments, not required blockers for creating an item.
Course pages and Explore pages should reference the same concept IDs so a learner can move between lesson context and system-level explanations.
User-created content should use the same vocabulary/grammar shapes where possible.
